description.old: Verify a first-time third-party user can log in and the system creates an associated Website account. Run for each of the 5 confirmed providers (Google, Facebook, X, Tiktok, wechat) as separate executions.
description.new: [Revised 2026-06-02] Verify a first-time third-party user completes OAuth → Link Your Account binding flow → a new platform account is created and the OAuth identity is linked. PRD §3.2.2 (2026-05-26) added an explicit intermediate Link Your Account page; this case now covers that step. Run for each of the 5 providers (Google, Facebook, X, TikTok, WeChat) as separate executions or via AUTH-059..063.

steps.old:
1. Open login.
2. Choose provider.
3. Authorize.
4. Return to Website.
steps.new:
1. Open login page.
2. Click the third-party provider button (Google / Facebook / X / TikTok / WeChat).
3. Complete provider OAuth authorization.
4. Land on 'Link Your Account' page — Email mode by default.
5. Enter an UNREGISTERED email; solve captcha (动态码); click 'Get Code' to send OTP.
6. Retrieve OTP from inbox; enter Verification Code.
7. Tick the mandatory Privacy + Ticket Purchase Terms checkbox.
8. Click 'Link Account'.

expected.old:
1. Login succeeds.
2. Website account is created/associated using provider primary key.
3. Identity correct.
expected.new:
1. Provider OAuth succeeds.
2. Link Your Account page shows orange notice: 'This email is not registered. After verification, a new account will be created and linked to your <Provider> account.'
3. New platform account is created and the third-party identity is bound to it.
4. 'Account linked successfully' page shown; auto-login completes after ~2 seconds.
5. No duplicate account exists for this provider unique-id.

description.old: Verify an existing Website user logs in through associated third-party account without duplicate account creation. Run per provider as needed.
description.new: [Revised 2026-06-02] Verify third-party login with a provider whose unique-id is ALREADY linked → the Link Your Account page is SKIPPED and the user is logged in directly. PRD §3.2.2 step 5.a: 若已绑定 直接登录成功. This case now explicitly asserts the skip.

steps.old:
1. Open login.
2. Choose provider.
3. Authorize.
4. Return.
steps.new:
1. Prerequisite: provider unique-id is already linked to a platform account from a previous run.
2. Open login page.
3. Click the same provider button.
4. Authorize via the same provider account.

expected.old:
1. Login succeeds to existing account.
2. No duplicate.
expected.new:
1. Provider OAuth succeeds.
2. Link Your Account page is NOT shown (skipped because provider unique-id is already bound).
3. User is logged in directly to the existing platform account.
4. Third-party user info (nickname / email) is re-synced to the platform per PRD §3.2.2.

description.old: Verify a Website user can log in via Google (OAuth 2.0 redirect) end-to-end: first-time creates an associated Website account; subsequent logs into the same account. Runs as a dedicated case so each provider has explicit coverage (mindmap lists all 5 providers as named branches).
description.new: [Revised 2026-06-02] Google OAuth end-to-end: first-time flow now includes the Link Your Account binding page (see AUTH-078 for the new-account branch, AUTH-079 for the already-registered-email branch). Subsequent login with same Google account skips Link page (covered by AUTH-018 + AUTH-087).

steps.old:
1. Open login.
2. Choose Google.
3. Authorize using a Google test user not yet associated.
4. Verify login + account creation.
5. Log out.
6. Repeat the flow with the same Google account.
steps.new:
1. Open login.
2. Choose Google.
3. Authorize using a Google sandbox account whose unique-id is not yet linked.
4. On Link Your Account page, complete email-mode binding (or switch to phone).
5. Verify login succeeds + account created.
6. Log out.
7. Repeat steps 1-3 with the same Google account.

expected.old:
1. First-time Google login authorises and creates / associates a Website account using the Google primary key.
2. Subsequent Google login logs into the same account; no duplicate is created.
3. Identity displayed matches the Google profile per approved mapping.
expected.new:
1. First-time Google login passes through Link Your Account, creates a platform account, links Google unique-id.
2. Subsequent Google login bypasses Link page and lands directly on home (PRD §3.2.2 step 5.a).
3. No duplicate platform account is created.
4. Identity (nickname / email) matches Google profile.
